harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2, and node3 (initial standbys) on Ubuntu 16.04. Demonstrated full failover: rebooted node1 to simulate primary loss, promoted node2 (the synchronous standby, guaranteeing zero data loss) to writable primary, reattached node3 to node2, then reattached the recovered former primary node1 to node2 as a standby with all committed data intact. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all three nodes (node1's restart doubled as the failover trigger), proving changed boot identity and full service/data/cluster-membership recovery on each. Final state: node2 is primary with node1 (sync) and node3 (async) both streaming correctly, all 3 committed rows present everywhere.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 9.5 + contrib on node1, node2, node3 (worked around a flaky apt mirror by copying cached .deb packages from node1 to node2 via SSH and installing with dpkg)
Generated a replicator role and password on node1; configured node1 as primary (listen_addresses, wal_level, max_wal_senders, wal_keep_segments, hot_standby, pg_hba.conf) and restarted
Took pg_basebackup of node2 and node3 from node1 with -R, enabled hot_standby, verified streaming replication and data propagation (repl_test table)
Set synchronous_standby_names='node2' on node1 with synchronous_commit=on to guarantee zero data loss on failover, verified sync_state=sync
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, uptime, pg_is_in_recovery, replication status, table contents) on all three nodes
Inserted a synchronously-committed row on node1, disabled postgresql autostart on node1 to prevent split-brain, then rebooted node1 to simulate primary loss
Promoted node2 via pg_ctl promote, verified zero data loss and writability with a new insert, then configured node2's postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf as a full primary and restarted
Rebuilt node3 via fresh pg_basebackup from node2 (needed due to a stale wal_level=minimal record on the timeline-2 branch point) and pointed its recovery.conf at node2; verified streaming and data
After node1 rebooted, rebuilt it via fresh pg_basebackup from node2 and configured recovery.conf to follow node2 as a standby; verified data intact and re-enabled postgresql autostart
Reconfigured synchronous_standby_names='node1' on node2 (new primary) for continued zero-data-loss protection
Executed mandatory restart protocol: rebooted node2 (current primary) and node3, polling boot_id/uptime for change and verifying full replication/data recovery after each, one node at a time

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication established: node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys, data replicating
evidence.summary: node1 configured with wal_level=hot_standby, max_wal_senders=10; node2 and node3 base-backed up from node1 and confirmed pg_is_in_recovery=t; a row inserted on node1 appeared on both standbys

evidence.requirement: Synchronous replication configured to guarantee no committed-data loss on failover
evidence.summary: synchronous_standby_names='node2' set on primary; pg_stat_replication shows node2 sync_state=sync

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured pre-disruption on all 3 nodes
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, uptime -s, pg_is_in_recovery, replication state, and repl_test contents on node1/node2/node3 before any disruption

evidence.requirement: Primary loss simulated; standby promotes to writable primary without losing committed data
evidence.summary: Committed row 2 synchronously on node1, rebooted node1 (ack returned before disconnect), promoted node2 via pg_ctl promote, verified both prior rows present plus successful new write on node2

evidence.requirement: Other standby (node3) reattached to new primary without data loss
evidence.summary: node3 rebuilt via base backup from node2 and confirmed streaming with all 3 rows present; node2's pg_stat_replication shows node3 streaming

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary (node1) rejoins as standby of the new primary (node2), no data loss
evidence.summary: Confirmed postgresql did not auto-start on node1 post-reboot (preventing split-brain), rebuilt node1 via base backup from node2, started as standby, verified pg_is_in_recovery=t with all 3 rows present, and re-established synchronous replication with node1

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node1 (boot identity change + recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b185f188... captured, reboot acknowledged, post-reboot boot_id 1c05113a... confirmed changed, postgresql correctly stayed down (disabled) then manually rejoined as standby with data verified

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node2 (boot identity change + recovery, including cluster membership as primary)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6ab98831... and healthy primary state captured, reboot acknowledged, post-reboot boot_id 56fde91e... confirmed changed, postgresql auto-started as primary with both standbys (node1 sync, node3 async) reconnected and data intact

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node3 (boot identity change + recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 225ffbf7... and standby state captured, reboot acknowledged, post-reboot boot_id 60a16f0d... confirmed changed, postgresql auto-started as standby of node2 with all data intact

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster health check after all restarts
evidence.summary: node2 confirmed as primary (pg_is_in_recovery=f) with node1 (sync) and node3 (async) both streaming; node1 confirmed as active standby (pg_is_in_recovery=t)
